mechanism_narrative: Persistent GROCERY_PHARM elevation (22.4–30.1% above baseline over four weeks) indicates sustained essential-goods demand that anchors foot traffic to mixed-use retail zones, mechanically lifting RETAIL_REC through co-location effects over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM sustained 22–30% above baseline across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 15% above baseline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility collapsed from −10.4% to −33.4% in week t-1w, signaling a sharp work-from-home shift or lockdown onset. This shock triggers compensatory leisure-time substitution, driving RETAIL_REC recovery as workers redirect time to recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 20 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following the WORKPLACES shock, or WORKPLACES rebounds to above −15% within one week of the shock.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage remains suppressed (−10.7% to −2.4% over four weeks) while RESIDENTIAL elevation persists (5.0–8.7%), indicating constrained commute capacity. When TRANSIT recovers above −5%, commuter confidence returns and retail foot traffic follows within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above −5% from a baseline below −8%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT averaged −5.6% over four weeks; RESIDENTIAL averaged 6.0%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week of TRANSIT crossing −5%, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 2% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains deeply suppressed (−21.6% to −25.4% across four weeks), indicating outdoor recreation constraints (weather, policy, or safety concerns). Sustained park closure diverts leisure demand to indoor retail venues, sustaining RETAIL_REC depression over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS consistently −21% to −25% below baseline across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above the last 28-day mean when PARKS remains below −20%, or PARKS recovers above −10% without a corresponding RETAIL_REC decline.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at −12% to −14% over four weeks despite volatile WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals, indicating policy-imposed capacity caps or operating-hour restrictions. This regime persists over the next four weeks, preventing RETAIL_REC recovery regardless of demand-side shifts.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC variance remains below 3 percentage points across four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC ranged only −10.1% to −14.0% across four weeks (3.9 pp range)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks, or WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover above −5% without RETAIL_REC moving.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (5.0–8.7% above baseline) combined with suppressed TRANSIT (−2.4% to −10.7%) creates a home-centric regime. When both signals persist, consumers shift to online shopping and delivery, depressing RETAIL_REC foot traffic over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 4% AND TRANSIT below −5% simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases when RESIDENTIAL and TRANSIT maintain their current regime, or TRANSIT recovers above −2% without RESIDENTIAL falling below 3%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC are co-located in mixed-use districts. When GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 25% above baseline (weeks t-2w and t-1w at 30.1% and 28.7%), spillover foot traffic to adjacent retail occurs with a one-week lag, lifting RETAIL_REC in week t+1w.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 25% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following GROCERY_PHARM peaks above 25%, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 20% before RETAIL_REC responds.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are leading indicators of commute resumption. When both rise simultaneously above −10%, office workers return and weekday retail traffic follows within one week. Current suppression (WORKPLACES −18.6%, TRANSIT −2.4%) predicts continued RETAIL_REC depression over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain below −10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above −10% when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below −10%, or both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover above −8% without RETAIL_REC rising.
